severity rationale: The timeout overload is not used by the current production ADS7066 path, so it does not directly affect deployed acquisition; it remains broken for any future timeout-path caller.
cause: The timeout overload performs separate HAL transmit and receive operations instead of one simultaneous transaction.
impact: A device response clocked during the transmit phase is discarded, so command/response alignment is wrong for full-duplex SPI devices that use this overload.
expected correction: Reject unequal lengths and call HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive once with the caller's timeout.

severity rationale: Production currently selects manual acquisition, so this defect is dormant in the deployed loop; autonomous mode is not ready to enable.
cause: configureAutonomousMode asserts SEQ_START before programming the operating rate, oversampling, and output format.
impact: If autonomous mode is enabled, the ADC can begin a scan with reset or stale settings and return samples with unexpected timing or format.
expected correction: Program OPMODE_CFG, OSR_CFG, and DATA_CFG before the SEQUENCE_CFG write that asserts SEQ_START.

severity rationale: Production currently selects manual acquisition, so this defect is dormant in the deployed loop; autonomous reads are not ready to enable.
cause: readChannelAuto passes its receive buffer through a full-duplex receive path, causing old response bytes to be clocked on MOSI.
impact: If autonomous mode is enabled, a prior ADC result can be interpreted as a command and corrupt configuration or result sequencing.
expected correction: Use an explicitly initialized zero-filled NOP transmit buffer for every automatic-result transfer.

severity rationale: The current production publisher does not invoke the priority API, so it does not directly affect deployed traffic; the API silently drops messages if adopted.
cause: transmitPriorityMessage unconditionally returns success without creating a header, selecting priority, or calling the HAL.
impact: A future caller would believe a priority frame was accepted even though no CAN frame was queued or transmitted.
expected correction: Implement priority transmission with a valid classic-CAN header, queue-capacity handling, HAL status propagation, and a real completion result.

severity rationale: The deployed publisher (BoardManager::fdcan_tx) only uses checkACK's boolean result as an aggregate TX-buffer-drain check after a fixed delay; it does not attribute completion to a specific enqueued frame, so the missing per-request buffer-index correlation does not change the deployed pass/fail decision.
cause: checkACK does not retain the hardware transmit-buffer index for each request and therefore cannot correlate TXBRP/TXBTO state to one message.
impact: Interleaved or wrapped transmissions can be reported with the wrong ACK state, undermining delivery diagnostics and fault handling.
expected correction: Record the buffer/request identity returned at enqueue time and evaluate completion and cancellation bits only for that request.

severity rationale: The ignored HAL return mainly leaves diagnostic error-code/counter output stale; it also affects the status.BusOff-triggered auto-restart, but worst case there is a spurious or missed restart attempt, not a masked delivery failure, since the FIFO-drain result fdcan_tx actually acts on comes from direct TXBRP/TXBTO register reads unaffected by the unchecked call.
cause: checkACK ignores return values from HAL_FDCAN_GetProtocolStatus and HAL_FDCAN_GetErrorCounters.
impact: Uninitialized or stale protocol data can be treated as valid, masking bus-off, ACK failure, or counter-read failure.
expected correction: Check both HAL return values, stop evaluation on failure, and return a distinct failure result before reading either output structure.

severity rationale: The helper is outside the normal all-channel publication path, but malformed callers can read and publish the wrong ADC.
cause: pushChannel treats every adc_num other than 1 as ADC2 instead of accepting only identifiers 1 and 2.
impact: An invalid identifier silently samples ADC2 and labels that value with the caller's CAN ID.
expected correction: Reject adc_num values outside 1 and 2 before any SPI or CAN activity.

severity rationale: CAN ID 700 is a deployed data contract, and the current source assignments conflict with the DBC signal roles.
cause: push_on_bus maps front oil-temperature ADC channels into ID 700 fields that the DBC names Engine_Temperature and Gearbox_Temperature.
impact: Consumers receive plausible but semantically wrong values and cannot distinguish engine/gearbox temperature from wheel oil temperature.
expected correction: Obtain the missing released physical source mapping, then bind ID 700 to those approved channels; do not guess replacement channels.

severity rationale: Brake-line channels are mapped as PT1000 inputs, while production dispatches them to a different conversion helper.
cause: Both brake-line paths call GE1711_function even though the mapping identifies the channels as PT1000.
impact: Published brake-line values are produced by a conversion that does not match the mapped sensor class.
expected correction: After the exact PT1000 part, table, divider population, and wiring are released, implement that approved conversion and dispatch both brake-line channels to it.

severity rationale: The deployed main loop can publish after an explicit ADC health failure.
cause: The main while(1) loop records BoardManager_checkADCPower in ok but gates publication only on BoardManager_updateData.
impact: Publication proceeds without distinguishing a failed health check from a healthy acquisition cycle.
expected correction: Require both the health result and the update result before calling BoardManager_push_on_bus, and expose the degraded state.

severity rationale: The deployed transmit path now retries a transient transmit failure once within push/fdcan_tx (draining the stuck queue-head message so the publish cycle stays in sync) and logs the failing CAN ID on the serial console for visibility; the residual gap is aggregate bus-level failure propagation and a degraded-publication policy across the frame set, accepted as a non-blocking advisory for the current deployment because a sustained fault still falls back to checkACK's bus-off restart.
cause: push_on_bus discards every bool result returned by BoardManager::push and has no frame-set failure policy.
impact: Individual frame failures do not stop, invalidate, or report the publication cycle at the board-manager level, so partial telemetry can still appear successful to bus consumers.
expected correction: Propagate per-frame failures from push_on_bus and implement the approved retry, delay, and degraded-publication policy.

severity rationale: An in-service ADC reset can silently invalidate a complete sensor scan.
cause: The production scan checks transfer success but does not verify ADC configuration or detect a reset during acquisition.
impact: Post-reset register defaults can change channel/result interpretation while the loop continues publishing the samples as valid.
expected correction: Detect reset/configuration loss during the bounded scan, invalidate the cycle, reconfigure the ADC, and suppress publication until recovery.
source location: Core/Src/main.c :: main while(1) loop; Core/Src/BoardManager.cpp :: BoardManager::updateData

severity rationale: The reproduced difference is a bounded endpoint-normalization convention; the installed RE22 variant, direction, and mechanical zero remain unknown, so the full physical conversion cannot yet be judged.
cause: RE22_function divides by 65535 and hard-codes an unverified 360-degree transfer.
impact: The SIL characterizes the current midpoint/endpoint arithmetic, while actual direction, travel, and zero error remain indeterminate until the fitted variant is identified.
expected correction: Obtain the installed RE22 ordering code and calibrated zero, then implement its documented electrical travel, direction, ADC code width, and approved endpoint convention.

severity rationale: The directly tested conversion helper has undefined endpoint handling and can return non-finite values to any caller.
cause: GE1711_function divides by 3.3 V minus the reconstructed input and evaluates logarithms without endpoint guards.
impact: Direct zero/full-scale helper inputs can produce NaN or infinity; this defect does not by itself establish which production sensor should dispatch to GE1711_function.
expected correction: Add finite endpoint guards and implement the approved GE1711 divider/calibration only after the population and wiring are released.
